blocks.h: Decisions to settle before the URS is approved
blocks.intro: Most water findings we fix were set at design, before the user requirement specification (URS) was approved.

items.t: Product mix now and in five years
items.d: We size generation and headers for the lines you plan, plus any still and pure steam generator feed, and write expansion into the URS.
USP stage 1 conductivity is tighter for PW; Ph. Eur. adds nitrates and its own microbial method. Both: cheap at design, costly later.
Both are pharmacopoeial. Distillation fills a hot loop and has the longer inspection record; membrane uses less energy but needs a stronger control strategy.
Annex 1 gives hot circulation above 70 °C as its WFI example. PW loops often run ambient with hot water or ozone sanitization.
Feed swings from near freezing in winter to over 20 °C in summer; some supplies use chloramine. We size membranes at your coldest month.
Duplex trains and isolable loop sections let you sanitize, service or tie in points of use without stopping every line.

blocks.h: What we do, URS to service

items.d: URS review, mass balance at your coldest and warmest feed, functional specification and design qualification support.
Wet factory acceptance testing (FAT) to a protocol you approve, then site acceptance testing (SAT) on your feed.
Installation and operational qualification (IQ/OQ) to protocols your quality unit approves, then support through PQ.
316L product-contact piping with weld logs, borescope records and mill-heat material certificates.
Plans with stated response times, USP <645> and <643> instrument calibration, reports for your GMP records.
Capacity, online TOC, sanitization and controls upgrades on any builder's system, requalification scope stated first.

blocks.h: Questions engineering, validation and QA leads ask

items.a: Usually not. The EMA guideline sets PW as the minimum for oral, cutaneous, nasal, ear, rectal and vaginal products and for granulation and coating. The exceptions are products that must be sterile and non-pyrogenic, such as some nebuliser solutions. USP publishes no equivalent table: your registration and specification decide.

items.q: Can one system supply Canada, the United States and Europe?
items.a: Yes. We design to the stricter of USP and Ph. Eur. on each attribute, test both at FAT where the methods allow it, and write both into the functional specification, so the same records answer Health Canada, the FDA and an EU importer.

items.q: Is membrane WFI acceptable to Health Canada and the FDA?
items.a: USP allows WFI by distillation or a process shown equivalent or superior to it; Ph. Eur. 0169 has allowed reverse osmosis with other techniques since April 2017. Health Canada applies the pharmacopoeia in your product file. For EU markets, notify the GMP supervisory authority before use. Confirm the route product by product with your regulatory team.

items.q: Do natural health products need USP Purified Water?
items.a: GUI-0158 sets potable water as the minimum. Many NHP makers move to PW for liquids, for products whose specification names a pharmacopoeial grade, or when microbial results over shelf life call for it. A PW skid on the same platform as a drug-grade system can be qualified to the level your product needs.

items.q: Does a new production line mean full requalification?
items.a: Not normally. The change goes through your change control, and a risk assessment sets the scope: usually IQ and OQ for the new section and a period of increased sampling at the new points of use. We state that scope before the first cut and plan the tie-in around your shutdown.

items.q: Can we use the water during PQ?
items.a: WHO TRS 1033 Annex 3 allows use in phase 2 of PQ with quality unit approval, after a first phase of at least two weeks with no manufacturing use. Your validation master plan decides. The commissioning and qualification page sets out each phase.
